criterion_notes.c1: Examines rural drinking water services (Rural Potable Water / APR community-managed systems) in Chile, focusing on system sustainability, functionality, tariff adequacy, and connection expansion.
criterion_notes.c2: Under the plain wording of Criterion 2, this paper would satisfy Criterion 2 because it examines rural water governance structures and reviews Chile's Law No. 20.998 (2017). Under the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading, it fails as an empirical rule-type analysis: the empirical component (a 2016 Delphi survey conducted prior to the 2017 law) only asks experts to rate the general importance of 34 broad operational, environmental, financial, and macro-governance sustainability drivers (e.g., water resource availability, CWO management, operator capacity, adequate tariffs, broad regulatory/legal framework), while the specific rule-type mechanisms in Law No. 20.998 (tariff structures covering operating costs, 5-year CWO licensing requirements, restrictions on municipal operation, and Article 89 enforcement sanctions) were enacted after data collection and are examined only via prospective policy commentary with no empirical implementation data.
criterion_notes.c3: Contains primary empirical data from a structured 4-round Delphi survey conducted in 2016 with 14 Chilean rural water sector experts (reporting non-parametric consensus statistics, rankings, and brief qualitative expert comments). Secondary coverage and functionality figures in Section 2.1 are background literature citations rather than primary analysis or a systematic synthesis.
criterion_notes.c4: Fails Criterion 4: the primary empirical outcome reported is expert Likert-scale importance ratings (1 to 5) and consensus scores on 34 perceived drivers of rural water system sustainability (Table 1), rather than an empirical measure or socio-legal documentation of household or community water access, connection, service availability, reliability, continuity, quantity, affordability, or exclusion outcomes.
criterion_notes.c5: Fails Criterion 5: the empirical sample consists of 14 national rural water experts rating candidate sustainability factors in 2016, with no identifiable empirical exposure-to-access-outcome linkage (Law No. 20.998 was passed in 2017 after the survey and was still in its 3-year implementation window).

evidence_quotes.quote: We draw our insights from a Delphi analysis conducted in 2016, prior to the passage of the new law asking Chilean rural water sector experts to identify factors that influence the sustainability of rural water service delivery in Chile.

The new regulation aims to strengthen the management capacity of community organizations, address deficits in tariffs through implementing a tariff structure covering service operation, establish stronger rights and obligations for CWOs and operators, and strengthen the ability of the central government to enforce norms.
Using these criteria, we identified 23 experts, 14 of whom agreed to participate in the study.
Round 2 required experts to rate factor importance on a Likert scale of 1 (not important) to 5 (very important).

Further research to trace the implementation of Law No. 20.998 and identify the conditions under which CWOs are more likely to be in line with the new law will help to provide insights for countries that, like Chile, want to address the inequities of quality and challenges of sustainability in rural water services.

raw_response.exposure: not reported (the 2016 Delphi survey elicits expert importance ratings across 34 general rural water sustainability drivers rather than evaluating an empirical exposure; Law No. 20.998 of 2017 is discussed only prospectively prior to implementation)
raw_response.outcome: Expert Likert-scale importance ratings (1 to 5) and consensus rankings of 34 perceived drivers of rural water system sustainability (no empirical household or community service access outcome measured)
raw_response.population_and_sample: 14 Chilean rural water sector experts (4 academics, 1 lawyer in rural water rights, 2 private water service consultants, 1 water committee member, and 5 government officials) out of 23 invited experts
raw_response.rationale: Excluded as E04 (Wrong outcome). Although the paper addresses rural drinking water services in Chile and includes a primary 2016 4-round Delphi survey of 14 sector experts alongside a prospective policy discussion of Law No. 20.998 (2017), its empirical component measures only expert consensus and Likert importance scores across 34 general drivers of rural water system sustainability rather than any empirical household or community outcome of water access, connection, availability, reliability, continuity, quantity, affordability, or exclusion. Moreover, because the Delphi survey was conducted in 2016 before Law No. 20.998 was enacted in 2017, the paper contains no empirical data on how the statute's rule-type provisions (tariff rules, 5-year CWO licensing, municipal operation limits, and enforcement fines) affect service access. Thus, the paper is excluded under both the narrow 2026-10-13 reading and the plain wording of Criterion 2.
raw_response.study_design: Four-round Delphi expert consensus survey (n = 14 experts) paired with prospective policy commentary on Law No. 20.998
